storage_form: PROVISIONAL. A flat table, deliberately. The atomic claims confirmed on 2026-09-17 now live in kb/entries/ and are cited from the rows below as entry_ref; this table stays as the machine-readable index the microscope agent reads directly (plan.md 4.3.0), because the entry schema has no structured slot for identifiers such as a part number or a slot position. See README.md in this folder.

verification.who: the operator (kyuhwan), row by row at the instrument
verification.standing_decision: every confirmed_by stamp that predated that pass was treated as unverified until re-affirmed item by item. A stamp applied in bulk records less than it claims.
verification.what_it_changed: one channel was a phantom and is gone (camera_splitter), one was never connected and is not a control channel (temperature_stage), two pairs of elements were one mechanism each, and the six objectives are now on the nosepiece.

stamp_audit.why: The pass of 2026-09-17 decided that every confirmed_by stamp predating it was unverified until re-affirmed item by item, because a stamp applied in bulk records less than it claims. The first version of this table carried that stamp on nine channels while the pass had actually gone through five of them. The other four kept a confirmation nobody had given -- which is the same defect as a self-reported grade, one level up.
stamp_audit.what_changes_and_what_does_not: No grade moves: a prior-project fact and an operator reading are both capped at E3. What changes is the dependency. confirmed_meaning below says a stamped row can survive the other repository disappearing; an unstamped one cannot, and these five cannot. Re-reading any of them at the instrument restores the stamp one row at a time.
stamp_audit.not_a_retraction: widefield_source_a and widefield_source_b are a stronger case than the other three: their stamp is removed AND the claim it covered is demoted to a gap, because the prior project recorded that its own measurement cannot distinguish the two assignments. The other three are simply unconfirmed here.

grade_cap_reason: plan.md 10.3 rule 1: a measurement taken in another project is not a measurement taken here. An operator reading is capped there too -- there is no run_id and no reproducible calibration state. Confirming any of these with a run promotes it to E1.
kept_fields_only: id, role, driver, automatable, read_back, lock_group, elements, exclusive_with, source, grade, entry_ref. Everything else in the source dossier -- serials, firmware versions, verification dates, and the narrative of how each fact was corrected -- was dropped: no consumer reads it.

consumers.a4: axis A4 screens configurations on automatable and read_back
consumers.o1_preflight: reads back every element it is about to set; read_back false means the element cannot be verified and goes to a manual instruction sheet (2.1 rule 5)
consumers.orchestrator: one worker per channel; lock_group compiles into the locks
consumers.a6: reads working distance and immersion off the nosepiece rows

light_engines.why: which of widefield_source_a and widefield_source_b is which engine is the open lapp_branch_assignment gap. Attaching these facts to a channel id would make them inherit that dispute; attached to a designation they are usable today.

installed.channels_from: the vendor designation itself: 8-NII-XS. Read off the loaded device list, not counted from icons.

light_engines.what_this_settles: a three-way disagreement about the Aura. A distributor page claiming 3 independently selectable channels is wrong for THIS unit; the dossier's icon count of 5 agrees with the designation. The designation wins because it is the device document (10.3 rule 2) and the icon count and the distributor page are not.

So this is an 8-channel engine whose channel set is unread -- see the light_engine_channel_sets gap. A count is not a list, and having the count makes it tempting to assume the standard set fills it.

serial_ports.what_it_cost_when_wrong: a configuration pointing the Lumencor adapter at COM4 hung about thirty minutes waiting for a reply that cannot come -- the piezo is not going to answer a Lumencor probe. A wrong COM number does not fail fast.

channels.role: microscope body: objective and filter turrets, output port, intermediate magnification, focus, transmitted lamp

elements.id_note: each objective's id IS its nominal magnification, a string identifier that is exact by definition (5.3). There is deliberately no numeric magnification field: a field for it is where a value back-derived from a calibrated pixel size ends up wearing a nominal name, which is what happened in the prior project's 20.078x.

objectives.wd_note: quoted as a range because it depends on the correction collar. wd_mm is null rather than a midpoint: with the coverslip fixed at 170 um the collar setting is determined and the working distance IS a single value, but the catalog does not publish it and the librarian does not interpolate inside a quotation (4.3). A null is loud; an interpolated number would be silent. See the gap objective_40x_wd_at_170um.

objectives.product: CFI Plan Apo Lambda D 60X Oil
CFI Plan Apo Lambda D 100X Oil

objectives_source.not_here: transmission at 1064 nm. The catalog publishes a curve and no numeric table, and a number a model reads off a rendered curve is E6, which may enter nothing (5.3). See the gap objective_transmission_1064nm.

elements.note: focus stabilisation; disabled across turret and path changes (2.1 interlock 3)

selects which widefield source reaches the sample. WHICH engine each state selects is not confirmed. This is also the one element on this instrument with a recorded history of an inverted label-to-state mapping -- see label_warning in optical_paths.v0.json, where a branch selector read back consistently wrong for weeks and only an image showed which position passed light. The element with that history is the element whose engine assignment is unverified, and those two facts are worth reading together rather than one at a time.

the focus axis. The channel role said FOCUS and no element was one, while the store asserted at E3 that smaller Z is retracted -- motion claimed and the mover unaddressed. MM label `ZDrive`, read from code positions and not from the relay; it is in the entry rather than here because every id in this table is this store's own name and not a device label. READ_BACK IS THE ELEMENT'S OWN and not the channel's: `core.getPosition("ZDrive")` appears at four call sites, so the position can be read after a move, which is what an interlock requiring verification == readback needs. LOCK_GROUP IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT -- see the gap. WHAT IT MOVES is not claimed: the document does not settle whether the objective or the sample carriage travels, and on an inverted stand that decides which way a collision closes.
elements.slot: the device registry element row, plus a KB entry. Consumer: O1 preflight and the turret-rotation interlock.

elements.note: coarse xy, on the body hub. Stage moves therefore serialise with port and filter changes under one channel, one worker (4.6.8) -- that consequence is design, not a hardware reading, and is not stamped as one.

channels.lock_note: The channel carries two lock groups. Its optical elements belong to optical_path; the motor stage belongs to stage, because the piezo rides on it. A lock group is therefore a property of an element, not only of a channel, and one worker for this channel can be blocked by two different locks: the lock a worker waits on is chosen per command, not per channel.

channels.role: spinning-disk confocal unit: excitation dichroic, disk in/out, spectral port to the two cameras, two emission wheels, shutter

elements.slot_contents: one dichroic fitted, in slot 1; slots 2 and 3 empty
elements.note: stays in the path whatever the disk does, which is why this instrument has no unfiltered white-light path. Its own spectral bands are not in the store.

the port IS the splitter: one mechanism that the configuration named twice. The split is spectral, not by intensity -- the two cameras see different bands, not the same image at half brightness. Two of the three states send zero light to one camera, so this is a selector that decides whether light arrives at all, and read-back cannot verify it: slot_order is null and commanding position 2 may land the mirror while read-back confirms position 2 and tells you nothing. Verify by acquiring (see label_warning in optical_paths.v0.json).
elements.not_entered: which arm is straight-through and which is reflected. That is a model's inference from the slot contents, which is E6 and may enter nothing (P2, 5.3). Read the dichroic's orientation or acquire a known emitter.

elements.note: gates the confocal laser into the unit; must be open while the confocal laser is in use. Which shutter an abort closes is policy, not knowledge: it belongs to a person in microscope_agent/envelope/safety.json (4.3.2, 10.3 rule 4). There are two shutters in this chain -- see laser_combiner/laser_shutter.

the operator said probably. Recalled, not read, so E5 while its neighbours are E3 -- and not promoted by the spectral splitter being consistent with it. If inverted, two-colour data is labelled wrong and nothing errors. One acquisition settles it: move one wheel and see which camera's image changes.
the complementary half of the same recalled claim, so it carries the same grade.
exposure must be an integer multiple of the disk period or stripes remain (axis A1); nothing acquires while the disk is still spinning up. The period itself is not in the store.

one mechanism, two names in the configuration: the confocal/bright-field selector and the disk in/out selector are the same thing. Disk-out is not a configuration of its own -- it is a required selector value on configurations that already exist. The position labelled bright field is also the widefield-fluorescence position, so the configuration id cannot be recovered from this label.

channels.element_count_note: seven elements. It was nine: two pairs were one mechanism each (port = splitter, disk position = bright), and the extractor had recorded each pair under both of its configuration names.

channels.role: detector on one arm of the spectral port. Named for the arm it sits on, not for a hardware difference.

channels.role: detector on the other arm of the spectral port. Same model as camera_red; primary and second were wiring and naming, not a hardware difference, and neither camera is the better one.
channels.source: mm_config, confirmed there by loading it
channels.note: identical models, so pixel size, quantum efficiency, read noise and full-well are the same on both arms and the two are photometrically comparable without a cross-calibration term. The 561 dichroic in the port is the only thing making the arms differ, which is why nothing about the cameras themselves can disambiguate the emission-wheel mapping.

elements.note: a shutter at the source, distinct from csuw1_shutter at the unit's entrance. This row records where it sits and what it gates. Which shutter an abort closes (2.1 interlock 1) is policy and is written by a person in envelope/safety.json -- the store cannot answer it and should not appear to.

open loop and NOT known to be calibrated: the device reports nothing back, and no calibration from command to output power is known to exist. A commanded power is therefore not a power figure, and nothing may present one as a milliwatt value. Abort never relies on a commanded power -- it closes a shutter, and which one is policy.
elements.calibrated_note: WAS `true` UNTIL 2026-09-24, and changed to the conservative reading because two records contradict it and a `calibrated` that is not is a power figure someone may trust. (1) The prior project's own record, kb/decisions/2026-09-02-lunf-first-light-measured-limits.md at a7b880b, section 4: every calibration record in the device database is empty, the milliwatt figure the acquisition software can show is a user-entered interpolation table, and volts to milliwatts is listed as still unknown. (2) This store's own entry lunf_per_line_power_is_not_transmittable says the combiner's power was already recorded as write-only and uncalibrated. Against them stands the operator reading of 2026-09-17 that this row was built from. Not resolved by this change: the person has been asked whether a calibration against a power meter exists. If one does, it comes back as a calibration source with its date and validity period, and this returns to true. Reported by manager-microscope-20260924-1 from card 036.

channels.driver: micromanager, device adapter MightexPolygon1000 (Mightex vendor package V1.0-202103)
channels.automatable_note: full ONLY on a core pinned to device interface 71. The row previously said automatable: full and named no core, and the property is core-dependent -- so a plan screened on it passes while the preflight that opens the device fails. The value stays full rather than becoming a new word like conditional, because A4 reads this field and no consumer knows a fourth value; an unknown value would fall through in an undefined direction, which is worse than a flagged one. That `automatable` has no way to say TRUE UNDER A PRECONDITION is raised with manager-librarian -- it is the same shape as automatable_gaps bundling can-be-set with can-be-verified.

core_requirement.loads_with: raw pymmcore pinned to device interface 71 (pymmcore==11.1.1.71.2), against the v71 Micro-Manager tree

core_requirement.match_rule: the check is EXACT MATCH, not a floor: a core requiring 75 refuses an adapter at 71 rather than accepting the older one. So this is not fixed by upgrading anything -- it is fixed by pinning the core down.
core_requirement.whole_config_loads: with the v71 core the prior project's full configuration loaded complete at 31 devices, the DMD included. The claim that this is the one device that does not load is true OF pymmcore-plus and false in general, and which of the two is the whole content of this row.
core_requirement.no_split_process_needed: a two-process design (DMD on v71, the rest on v75) was validated and works, and is unnecessary, because the full configuration loads on v71 in one process.

core_requirement.rule_passed: 10.3 rule 1: a run taken in another project is not a run taken here, so this caps at E3 however cleanly it was measured.

spectral_role.claim: the DMD chooses no colour. Its control surface takes an image -- an intensity per micromirror -- and has no wavelength parameter at all, so the band is chosen upstream by which light-engine line is lit. A plan that expects the DMD to pick a colour is asking a device to do something it exposes no way to do.
spectral_role.what_this_is_NOT: it is not a claim that the DMD passes every wavelength equally. Transmission through it is unmeasured -- see the dmd_spectral_transmission gap. Spectrally neutral conflates the two, and only the first half is established: no wavelength SELECTION, unknown wavelength-dependent LOSS.
spectral_role.slot: A4 -- device combination: the DMD cannot stand in for a line selector, which is a screening fact.
spectral_role.source: prior project run record 2026-09-07: the device is driven by writing an image to the SLM, and the per-line measurements were made by changing the light engine's line while a DMD pattern stayed displayed

channels.note: on the inline widefield branch only -- which is a fact about where the DMD is mounted, not about which engine shares that branch. Since the engine assignment is unconfirmed (gap lapp_branch_assignment), WHICH source the DMD patterns is unknown, and this is what makes that gap load-bearing rather than cosmetic: every patterned-illumination plan names a source.

gaps.what: which lock group the z_drive element belongs to
gaps.why_it_matters: a lock group schedules real motion. If z_drive is put in a group it does not belong to, moves serialise that need not and -- worse -- moves that must serialise may not
searched: the prior project at 34a432c, which has no lock-group concept at all. The nearest thing is COLLISION_DEVICES = {Nosepiece, ZDrive, PFSOffset}, and hardware/focus.py rules it out in its own words: ZDrive's membership in COLLISION_DEVICES guards writes to ZDrive PROPERTIES, not Z motion. So the one candidate the document offers is explicitly not about motion

manager-microscope reasoned it should serialise with rotation, because nosepiece_write_runs_no_escape says Z does not move on a software turret write. They flagged that as their own inference and it is not a registry value, so it is not taken
gaps.status: open. The element row is entered without the field rather than with a guess: a guessed lock group is not a missing fact, it is a false schedule for real motion, and nothing downstream would report it. WHAT WOULD CLOSE IT: the operator saying which moves on this stand must not run concurrently with a focus move -- a bench question and not a store question, and the answer is a person's rather than a document's.

gaps.what: the camera's settable exposure grid -- whether setExposure takes a continuum or snaps to a quantum, and what that quantum is
gaps.why_it_matters: a result card reporting planned 0.007 s and actual 0.008 s currently says `within_tolerance: true`, and check 72 returns UNDECIDED on it because nothing in contracts/ declares a tolerance. manager-simulation's reading is that this is not a tolerance at all but QUANTIZATION -- the device could not do otherwise -- and those are different claims: exact reproduction says there is no difference, a tolerance says the difference does not matter, quantization says no closer setting exists. Three claims in one boolean, and none of them checkable. With the grid on disk, `is actual the nearest settable point to planned` becomes a DERIVABLE verdict, the shape checks 6 and 72 already use.
searched: every camera_* entry in the store at kbv-a54fe073bef7: the four camera_read_noise_* rows carry read_noise and nothing else, so the line_time the grid might have been derived from is not there
the five handles a caller would reach for -- exposure_time, exposure, line_time, readout_time, frame_rate -- all return nothing

camera_red_mm_control_path, which answers HOW exposure is set and not WITH WHAT: `exposure and ROI are not device properties at all but core-level calls, setExposure and setROI`. That is itself part of the answer -- a core-level call has no property allowed-values list to read a grid off, so closing this means setting and reading back rather than querying
gaps.status: open, and NARROWER THAN IT LOOKS because the store already holds one exposure grid that is not the camera's. csuw1_disk_speed_exposure_constraint (E3, operator_read) says an exposure through the spinning disk must last AN INTEGER MULTIPLE OF THE DISK PERIOD or stripes remain -- quantization, stated as such, for the disk rather than the sensor. So the shape is already in the store and the missing one is the camera's. Note also interval_ms_is_ignored_and_frame_period_equals_exposure: the frame period equals the exposure exactly because readout is pipelined, so a frame-rate constraint reduces to an exposure one and this gap is the only place to close it. Raised by manager-microscope on 2026-09-21; recorded here rather than left in a message because the two other open questions it is to be bundled with -- what ends the pixel-size calibration, camera change and optical path -- have already outlived three sessions today.

gaps.status: HELD, which is not the same as absent and not the same as discarded. The measurements exist and are good; they attach to LINE LABELS, and the line labels are exactly what light_engine_channel_sets leaves unread. Entering them now would pin measurements to channels nobody has read. They also want an A1 or A2 slot that does not exist until the observable vocabulary does (11-1), and 10.2.1 discards an item that cannot name its slot -- holding is the honest third answer where discard would lose a good measurement and transfer would invent a slot. Released when the channel set is read.

the vendor designation we hold, which does not determine it: NPC-D is the CONTROLLER, and travel is a property of the stage
gaps.status: DISCARDED as a transfer, and open as a question for a person. 10.3 rule 4 makes safety limits non-transferable and 10.2's device-spec row stays shut until a human writes envelope/safety.json. The reason is not procedural: the prior project put that number in its safety document BECAUSE it was using it as a limit, and a travel range read as a permission is the exact failure the rule names. kind is inaccessible because the next action is the right one -- ask a person -- even though the barrier is a rule of this project rather than a paywall.

Queensgate's series is offered at 200, 400, 600 and 800 um, and 600 appearing in both that series and that SAFETY.md heading is a consistency, not a source. Picking the 600 because the number matches is inference, which is E6 and enters nothing.

gaps.what: the DMD's transmission, and whether it varies with wavelength

gaps.status: open. What IS established is narrower and is on the dmd row: the device selects no wavelength. That it therefore passes all of them equally does not follow and is not recorded. Closing this is a power measurement with the DMD in and out of the path, per line.

One acquisition settles it with no ambiguity -- illuminate, step the three slots, record which camera sees signal: empty gives red only, the 561 dichroic gives both, the 100/0 mirror gives blue only. Three distinguishable outcomes for three slots, which also confirms the contents independently of their labels.

gaps.what: the trapping laser's power AT THE SAMPLE
gaps.why_it_matters: it is what a sample sees, and it is what any statement about heating or about photodamage has to be in terms of. A7 owns the driving term and A3 owns sample health; both want this number and neither wants the generator's
searched: the operator, 2026-09-19: the laser is 1064 nm and the generator's maximum is 5 W, and the 20 percent of the detection bound is 20 percent of that. Those are facts about the GENERATOR
the prior project, which holds a measured output: NOT FETCHABLE, see the ruling below
the objective's transmission at 1064 nm, which would be one of the factors: itself an open gap (objective_transmission_1064nm)
gaps.status: open, and the tempting arithmetic is the thing to refuse. Twenty percent of five watts is one watt AT THE GENERATOR. Moving that number to the sample crosses losses nothing here records and an objective transmission that is itself unknown, and a figure that arrives at the sample carrying the generator's provenance is the failure this store keeps meeting under other names. Three facts, not one: the generator's rating, the generator's output at the time of the observation, and the power at the sample. Only the first is enterable today.
gaps.why_the_prior_measurement_cannot_be_fetc: 10.2's row for device spec values -- NA, magnification, pixel size, OUTPUT LIMITS -- waits on a human-written envelope/safety.json, which does not exist. The row states its own reason and it is this case exactly: a spec number not placed beside the limit values gets used as a limit. Same ruling as the piezo travel range (gap piezo_travel_range), reached the same way and for the same clause.
gaps.what_would_close_it: a measurement at the sample plane, with the dial position and the objective recorded beside it. Then the generator figure becomes an input to a ratio rather than a stand-in for the answer.

gaps.what: pixel size at the sample plane, per objective and intermediate magnification and binning
gaps.why_it_matters: every length read off an image depends on it, and it is what an observable's estimator needs to turn pixels into micrometres. Axis A6 is resolution, so this is the one A6 actually asked for
searched: not extracted from the prior project: a calibration taken elsewhere migrates capped at E3 and its calibration state cannot be reproduced here (10.3 rule 1)
not derivable from the sensor pitch: see must_not_derive
gaps.status: open, and it does not close when the sensor pitch arrives. Saying so is the point of this record: something called pixel_size will exist in the store soon and this gap is not the one it answers. A gap that closes for the wrong reason is worse than one left open, because nobody returns to it. A6 stays open.
gaps.must_not_derive: do not produce this by dividing the sensor pitch by a nominal magnification. The prior project's dossier holds exactly that artifact -- a 20.078x objective, which is 6.5 um over a calibrated um/px -- a calibrated quantity wearing a nominal name. 5.3's nominal rule refuses it from one side (a nominal designation is a string, not a number) and task 009's ruling from the other (nominal_magnification is an identifier, and identifiers do not enter numbers[]).
gaps.three_facts_one_name: sensor pitch, fixed, a vendor spec. Effective pitch, which is the sensor pitch times the binning factor, and nothing here records what binning this instrument runs. Sample-plane pixel size, which only a measurement on this instrument gives and which is E2 with a validity window when it comes. They are three and the word pixel_size covers all three.
gaps.measured_here_is_E2: when a person measures it, it arrives as a result card and this session turns it into an entry (rule 9). Nothing else is a path for it.

gaps.what: working distance of MRD77400 (40x-WI) at a coverslip thickness of exactly 170 um
gaps.why_it_matters: axis A6 wants a working distance, and for this lens the catalog gives an interval where fixing the coverslip determines a single value
searched: Nikon catalog row for MRD77400 -- quotes 0.16 to 0.2 mm, correction-collar dependent, for coverglass 150 to 190 um

nearest.uncovered: the collar setting that 170 um implies, and therefore which value inside 0.16 to 0.2 mm applies

gaps.status: open, and the KIND changed on 2026-09-22 while the gap stayed open. The condition is now not merely known but MET AND PINNED: the person read the collar at 0.17 mm and will leave it there (objective_40x_collar_setting, operator_read, E3), which confirms the inference that 170 um glass determines the setting. What is still missing is the value itself -- the catalogue quotes 0.16 to 0.20 mm for the WHOLE collar range and publishes nothing at 0.17, and the librarian does not interpolate inside a quotation. So this stopped being a condition_mismatch, which says the conditions do not line up, and became `absent`, which says they do and the number is not there. The second is the better state and it is not an answer. A caller that needs one number still takes the interval and records its own choice as an assumption, naming this gap. TWO USES AND ONLY ONE IS UNBLOCKED: the safety floor does not need it, because the person ruled fallback [working_distance_min] and 0.16 is the near end at any collar setting, so that ruling is untouched; autofocus does need it, because choosing an end is wrong by up to 40 um either way and at 40x water that is fully out of focus. WHAT CLOSES IT: focus on the coverslip interface and read the encoder -- measured here, which also clears 10.3 rule 1 E3 cap. The 018 bench visit already carries interface offsets for all six lenses, so it adds no visit.

gaps.what: whether the sample temperature stage will be connected, and what would drive it
gaps.why_it_matters: temperature enters every plan twice, through the thermal energy and through the viscosity, and without an actuator confirm mode has nothing to appeal to

gaps.what: the ambient sample temperature: its value, its drift band, and where it is read (room or near the sample)
gaps.why_it_matters: water's viscosity moves by roughly two percent per kelvin, so a drift band of a kelvin moves the diffusive time by the same amount -- invisible in explore mode, decisive in confirm mode
searched: plan.md 12 records 20 C with setpoint-or-measurement left undecided
operator pass of 2026-09-17, which settled that nothing actuates it
gaps.status: open, and narrowed three times. With nothing controlling the sample temperature the 20 C in plan.md 12 CANNOT be a setpoint, so it is an ambient value of the room. The operator stated on 2026-09-17 that he read it off a thermometer rather than recalling it, which settles the grade at E3 and puts the value in the store as entry lab_ambient_temperature. And on 2026-09-19 he answered WHERE: there is no thermometer beside the sample, and the one that exists reads the room. That was previously inferred from the absence of an actuator; it is now stated, which is a different and stronger claim. What is left is NOT the position but the two questions behind it -- how far the room thermometer sits from the sample, and how well the two track -- and neither is answered. Do not infer either: an unknown distance is not a small distance.

resolved_gaps.what: the Kinetix 22 sensor's pixel pitch, from the vendor datasheet
resolved_gaps.why_a_route_this_gap_had_ruled_closed_is: This gap's `searched` ruled the prior project CLOSED on 2026-09-19, and that ruling was right about the row it was about: 10.2's DEVICE-REGISTRY row covers control channels, automatability and read-back, and a sensor specification can name no slot in it. What resolved this is a DIFFERENT row -- 10.2's device-specification row, which names pixel size explicitly and was waiting on a person-written envelope/safety.json. That condition was met (c1404bf, extended beb1c98) and manager-librarian checked the table rather than the earlier message. A route closed for want of a slot and a route waiting on a condition are two things, and only the second one opened.
resolved_gaps.what_it_did_not_close: pixel_size_at_sample_plane, which stays open and said so in advance: `something called pixel_size will exist in the store soon and this gap is not the one it answers`. It was right. The entry carries the SENSOR pitch; the effective pitch needs the binning this instrument runs, and the sample-plane size needs a measurement here and arrives as E2 with a validity window.
resolved_gaps.the_route_this_gap_called_right_is_still: reading the datasheet PDF. What was read is agentic-microscope's transcription of it, marked `transcribed verbatim`, located under 10.3 rule 2, which calls the prior repository an index and not a source. The entry cites the datasheet and its source record says plainly that the sheet itself has not been read here.

resolved_gaps.what: which camera model is on each arm
resolved_gaps.note: both Kinetix 22. This closes a discrepancy the prior dossier left open between a purchase quote and the current state: a swap did happen against the quote, and the record now matches the hardware. The general lesson survives the specific resolution -- this instrument's paper record has drifted from its hardware before, which is why a position or model claim is re-read rather than inherited.

confirmed_meaning: confirmed_by means the fact no longer rests only on the prior project: the operator checked it here. The grade stays E3, since an operator reading is not a measurement by this system (10.3 rule 1), but the dependency on the other repository is gone and the row can survive that repository disappearing.
